These same nets also feed the hardware interlock transistors on page 3 (R2/FLOAT_LOW -> T1 base for the main pump, R11/FLOAT_HIGH -> T4 base for the ATO valve).
anomalies.expected: The reference netlist/SPICE deck specifies the opposite assignment: 'R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k, R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k' (spec §4.4), i.e. FLOAT_LOW pulled up and FLOAT_HIGH pulled down. With the float switches wired to GND (NC low-float, NO high-float), that gives the intended interlock: low water -> FLOAT_LOW high -> T1 on -> pump off; high water -> FLOAT_HIGH high -> T4 on -> valve off.

anomalies.impact: The pull-up/pull-down are swapped on both float channels, inverting the hardware safety interlocks. FLOAT_HIGH is held at +3V3 by default, keeping T4 conducting and the ATO valve gate pulled low, so the top-off valve stays closed when the tank is empty and opens only when the tank is full (overflow). FLOAT_LOW is held at GND, so T1 never turns on and the low-level pump cutoff is defeated. The board therefore behaves opposite to the intended ATO/pump-protection logic.
